answer: In a bonded-agent economy, each identity locks a jade stake, a slashable deposit, to hold one vertex in the work graph. Tasks are assigned by a verifiable random function weighted by stake, and a random auditor checks each result before payment. A Sybil cannot whisper fake results from many accounts: every new identity needs its own bond and joins the auditor pool, so the more clones it adds, the likelier one audits a fraudulent job, and one caught cheat slashes the whole linked stake. The attacker pays per identity and risks total forfeiture, so fake accounts never pay for themselves.
